medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot: Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot
Branch of the superficial fibular nerve to the medial part of the dorsum of the foot.
medial geniculate body: Thalamic relay nucleus of the auditory pathway; the auditory radiation goes from here to Heschl's gyrus.
medial occipitotemporal gyrus (parahippo: Gyrus beside the hippocampus; its anterior end curls into the uncus, the part that herniates in tentorial herniation.
medial pectoral nerve: Arises from the medial cord and supplies pectoralis minor and major.
medial plantar nerve: Sensation from the medial sole and the medial three and a half toes; supplies abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis (the foot's counterpart of the median nerve).
medial reticulospinal tract: Pathway from the pontine reticular formation that increases extensor tone.
medial sural cutaneous nerve: Branch of the tibial nerve that joins to form the sural nerve.
medial vestibulospinal tract: Descending pathway stabilising head and neck posture.
median nerve: Formed by the union of the lateral and medial cords; supplies most forearm flexors, the thenar muscles and the palmar skin of the lateral three and a half fingers. Compression in the carpal tunnel is the commonest entrapment neuropathy ('ape hand', 'hand of benediction').
medulla oblongata: Lowest part of the brainstem, continuous with the spinal cord at the foramen magnum. It contains the respiratory and circulatory centres, the nuclei of IX–XII and the pyramidal decussation.
meningeal branch of maxillary nerve: Small branch carrying sensation from the dura of the middle cranial fossa.
mental nerve: Branch leaving through the mental foramen and supplying the skin of the lower lip and chin.
midbrain: Part of the brainstem between the pons and diencephalon; formed by the tectum (colliculi), tegmentum (red nucleus, nuclei of III and IV) and the peduncles.
middle frontal gyrus: Its posterior part contains the frontal eye field (Brodmann 8); with damage the eyes look towards the side of the lesion.
middle temporal gyrus: Middle gyrus of the lateral surface of the temporal lobe.
motor nucleus of facial nerve: Nucleus supplying the muscles of facial expression; the part for the forehead muscles receives bilateral cortical control.
motor root of trigeminal nerve: Root passing below the ganglion to join the mandibular nerve and supply the muscles of mastication.
muscular branches of axillary nerve: Branches to deltoid and teres minor.
muscular branches of deep fibular nerve: Muscular branches of deep fibular nerve
Branches to the muscles of the anterior compartment.
muscular branches of median nerve: Branches to the muscles of the anterior compartment of the forearm.
muscular branches of radial nerve: Branches to triceps, brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus.
muscular branches of ulnar nerve: Branches to FCU and the ulnar half of FDP.
musculocutaneous nerve: Arises from the lateral cord and pierces coracobrachialis; supplies the anterior arm muscles and carries sensation from the lateral forearm.
nasolacrimal duct: Duct from the lacrimal sac opening into the inferior meatus; it may be blocked in newborns.
nerve to mylohyoid muscle: Branch supplying mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric.
nerve to quadratus femoris muscle: Branch supplying quadratus femoris and the inferior gemellus.
nodule of vermis: Vermian part of the flocculonodular lobe; the vestibulocerebellum.
nucleus ambiguus: Motor nucleus supplying the pharynx, larynx and soft palate (IX, X, XI); its lesion causes dysphagia and hoarseness (Wallenberg syndrome).
nucleus of abducens nerve: Beneath the facial colliculus in the floor of the fourth ventricle; it contains the lateral gaze centre.
nucleus of accessory nerve: Nucleus in the anterior horn of C1–C5 supplying sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
nucleus of hypoglossal nerve: Motor nucleus in the floor of the fourth ventricle supplying the tongue muscles.
nucleus of oculomotor nerve: At the level of the superior colliculus; supplies most eye muscles and levator palpebrae.
nucleus of solitary tract: Sensory nucleus receiving taste (VII, IX, X) and visceral sensation (baroreceptors, chemoreceptors).
nucleus of trochlear nerve: At the level of the inferior colliculus; its fibres cross and leave the back of the brainstem.
nucleus proprius: Main sensory nucleus of the dorsal horn.
obturator nerve: Arises from L2–L4 and passes through the obturator canal into the thigh; supplies the adductors. Its pain may be referred to the knee.
occipital pole: Most posterior tip of the hemisphere; macular vision is represented here.
occipitotemporal sulcus (lateral part*): Separates the inferior temporal and fusiform gyri.
oculomotor nerve (iii): Carries fibres to four eye muscles, levator palpebrae and the parasympathetic pupil fibres. In its palsy the eye turns down and out with ptosis and mydriasis; a posterior communicating aneurysm is a common cause.
olfactory nerve (i): Fibres from the olfactory epithelium passing through the cribriform plate to the olfactory bulb; anterior skull base fractures cause anosmia.
olfactory sulcus: Groove in which the olfactory bulb and tract lie.
olive: Oval swelling on the side of the medulla; the inferior olivary nucleus inside sends climbing fibres to the cerebellum.
opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus
With the triangular part it forms Broca's speech area (Brodmann 44); damage in the dominant hemisphere causes motor aphasia.
ophthalmic nerve: First, sensory division of the trigeminal; supplies the forehead, bridge of the nose and cornea and is the afferent limb of the corneal reflex. In herpes zoster ophthalmicus, involvement of the nose tip (Hutchinson sign) suggests eye involvement.
optic chiasm: Where the optic nerves meet; the fibres from the nasal retina cross. Compression by a pituitary tumour causes bitemporal hemianopia.
optic nerve (ii): Axons of retinal ganglion cells; it passes through the optic canal and, being wrapped in meninges, shows papilloedema when intracranial pressure rises.
optic tract: Visual pathway from the chiasm to the lateral geniculate body; its damage causes contralateral homonymous hemianopia.
orbital gyri: Inferior surface of the frontal lobe above the orbit; involved in decision making and impulse control.
orbital gyri (frontomarginal gyrus and s: Gyrus on the lower margin of the frontal pole.
orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus: Orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus
Part of the inferior frontal gyrus above the orbit.
orbital sulci (h-shaped orbital sulci*): Sulci on the orbital surface arranged like the letter H.
orbital sulci (lateral orbital sulcus*): Lateral sulcus of the orbital surface.
palmar branch of median nerve: Cutaneous branch passing above the carpal tunnel; this is why thenar skin sensation is preserved in carpal tunnel syndrome.
palmar branch of ulnar nerve: Cutaneous branch to the hypothenar skin.
paracentral gyrus and sulcus*: Continuation of the pre- and postcentral gyri on the medial surface; the motor and sensory area of the leg and foot (affected in anterior cerebral artery occlusion).
paracentral sulcus: Sulcus bounding the paracentral lobule in front.
parieto-occipital sulcus: Deep sulcus on the medial surface separating the parietal and occipital lobes.
peduncle of flocculus: White matter band connecting the flocculus to the nodule.
phrenic nerve: The only motor nerve to the diaphragm, from the cervical plexus (C3–C5, mainly C4). It descends on the front of scalenus anterior, enters the chest between the subclavian artery and vein and runs on the side of the pericardium in front of the lung root to the diaphragm; the right passes beside the superior vena cava, the left beside the aortic arch. Subdiaphragmatic irritation causes pain referred to the shoulder.
pons: Bulging part of the brainstem between the midbrain and medulla, connected to the cerebellum; contains the nuclei of cranial nerves V–VIII.
postcentral gyrus: Gyrus behind the central sulcus (Brodmann 3, 1, 2); perceives touch, pain and position sense from the opposite side.
postcentral sulcus: Sulcus bounding the postcentral gyrus behind.
posterior antebrachial cutaneous nerve: Sensation from the skin of the back of the forearm.
posterior branch of medial antebrachial: Posterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
Supplies the skin of the posteromedial forearm.
posterior branch of obturator nerve: Supplies obturator externus and adductor magnus.
posterior cochlear nucleus: One of the first brainstem relay nuclei of the auditory fibres.
posterior commissure: Crossing fibres below the pineal gland; they make the pupillary light reflex bilateral.
posterior cord of brachial plexus: Formed by the posterior divisions of the three trunks; gives the nerves supplying the extensors, mainly the axillary and radial nerves.
posterior division of inferior trunk of: Division that joins the posterior cord.
posterior division of mandibular nerve: Mostly sensory division; gives the auriculotemporal, lingual and inferior alveolar nerves.
posterior division of middle trunk of br: Division that joins the posterior cord.
posterior division of superior trunk of: Division that joins the posterior cord.
posterior femoral cutaneous nerve: Sensation from the skin of the back of the thigh and the gluteal fold.
posterior horn of spinal cord: Grey matter where sensory fibres synapse; the substantia gelatinosa takes part in pain modulation.
posterior interosseous nerve of forearm: Continuation of the deep branch; supplies the forearm extensors. Compression at the arcade of Frohse causes finger drop without sensory loss.
posterior nucleus of vagus nerve: Nucleus of the parasympathetic preganglionic fibres to the heart, lungs and digestive tract.
posterior quadrangular lobule: Uppermost hemispheric lobule of the posterior lobe.
posterior root of posterior femoral cuta: Posterior root of posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
Root of the nerve coming from the posterior divisions.
posterior segment of eyeball: Structures behind the lens (vitreous, retina, choroid).
posterior spinocerebellar tract: Starts in Clarke's nucleus and reaches the cerebellum of the same side through the inferior cerebellar peduncle.
posterolateral tract: Pathway in which pain and temperature fibres run up or down one or two segments before entering the dorsal horn.
precentral gyrus: Gyrus in front of the central sulcus (Brodmann 4); initiates voluntary movements of the opposite half of the body; the motor homunculus lies here.
precentral sulcus (inferior part)*: Lower part of the sulcus in front of the precentral gyrus.
precentral sulcus (superior part)*: Upper part of the sulcus in front of the precentral gyrus.
precuneus: Part of the parietal lobe on the medial surface in front of the cuneus; linked to visuospatial imagery and self-awareness.
proper palmar digital branches of median: Proper palmar digital nerves of median nerve
Sensory branches running along the sides of the fingers from the thumb to half of the ring finger.
proper palmar digital branches of ulnar: Proper palmar digital nerves of ulnar nerve
Sensory branches to the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger.
proper plantar digital branches of later: Proper plantar digital nerves of lateral plantar nerve
Sensation from the plantar surface of the lateral toes.
proper plantar digital branches of media: Proper plantar digital nerves of medial plantar nerve
Sensation from the plantar surface of the medial toes.
